title: Broad Classification of Industrial Occupancies into Different Degree of Hazard
extraction_method_and_confidence_warning: Like Table 7, Annex B is embedded as full-page RASTER IMAGES in the source .docx (3 portrait pages), not as editable text. Recovered via Tesseract OCR (upscaled 1.5x). OCR of this three-column, small-font list is generally legible but individual entries may contain misread characters (e.g. 'GCCUPANCIES' for 'OCCUPANCIES', 'Bakenies' for 'Bakeries') which have been corrected below where the intended word was obvious from context; a small number of column-boundary misreads (a term captured with an extra trailing/leading word from an adjacent column) are possible and this list should be spot-checked against the source PDF before production use, consistent with the 'needs_verification' flag the 2026 dataset also carries for its own Annex B.
terminology_note: 2016 labels its three columns 'Light Hazard', 'Moderate Hazard', and 'High Hazard' directly (not 'G-1/G-2/G-3'), but these map one-to-one onto the G-1 (Low/Light), G-2 (Moderate), G-3 (High) subdivisions defined in the classification clause (3.1.8) and used throughout Table 7's Industrial section.
usage_note: This Annex covers fire-hazard-only classification. Any occupancy not covered here shall be classified in the most appropriate class by resemblance to the proposed occupancy (identical rule to 2026's usage_note, worded almost identically).

Asbestos steam packing and lagging manufacturing
Cement factories and/or asbestos or concrete products manufacturing
Ceramic factories and crockery and stoneware pipe manufacturing
Coffee curing, roasting and grinding premises
Condensed milk factories, milk pasteurising plant and dairies
Electric lamps (incandescent and fluorescent) and TV picture tube manufacturing
Fruits and vegetables dehydrating and drying factories
Godowns and warehouses storing non-combustible goods only
Gum and/or glue and gelatine manufacturing
Ice, ice candy and ice-cream manufacturing
Water treatment/filtration plants and water pump houses
g2_moderate_hazard_examples: Bookbinders, envelopes and paper bag manufacturing
Carpenters, wood wool and furniture manufacturing
Chemical manufacturing using raw materials having flash points above 23 C
Coir carpets, rugs, tobacco, hides and skin presses
Electric generating stations (other than underground power houses)
Godowns and warehouses (other than light and high hazard categories)
Grain and/or seeds disintegrating and/or crushing factories
Hosiery, lace, embroidery and thread factories
Ink (excluding printing ink) factories - variant listing
Man-made yarn/fibre manufacturing (other than acrylic fibres/yarn manufacturing)
Manure and fertilizer works (blending, mixing and granulating)
Oil terminals/depots other than those categorised under High Hazard A
Open storage of flammable liquids in drums, cans, etc
Paper and cardboard mills without raw material yards
Piers, wharves, jetties and dockyards other than those categorized under High Hazard A

sub_category_a: Bituminised paper and/or hessian cloth/tar felt manufacturing
Chemical manufacturing using raw materials having flash points below 23 C
Cinema films and TV production studios
Coal and/or coke and/or charcoal ball and briquettes manufacturing
Foam plastics manufacturing and/or converting plants
Grass, hay, fodder and bhoosa (chaff) pressing factories
Industrial gas manufacturing (other than inert/halogenated hydrocarbon gases)
Metal or tin printers (where more than 50 percent of floor area is occupied as engineering workshop, may be taken as ordinary hazard risk)
Oil terminals/depots handling flammable liquids having flash point of 23 C and below
Paper and cardboard mills having raw material yards
Piers, wharves and jetties handling extra hazardous materials
g3_high_hazard_examples.sub_category_b_note: NOTE from source: 'In case of complexes having separate plants having varying degrees of hazard, authority having jurisdiction shall be consulted to decide on level of protection to be provided.'

entries_present_in_2026_annex_b_but_not_.note: These items appear in the NBCS 2026 dataset's annex_b_hazard_classification.json but were NOT found anywhere in the 2016 Annex B OCR output. Treated as genuine 2026 additions reflecting occupancy types that either did not exist, or were not separately hazard-classified, in 2016 - a concrete, useful delta for the product's edition-comparison logic.
new_hazard_categories_in_2026: Multiple block apartment buildings / Multiple block business buildings / Multiple block star hotel buildings (G-1/G-2) - cluster-building classification not present in 2016
QA/QC laboratories as a distinct duplicate entry, Electrical appliances manufacturing, Electronic products manufacturing (G-2) - not found in 2016

Indoor dry transformer room, MRI/scanning room, Network/electrical room, Operation theatre rooms, Optical goods facilities, Semiconductors manufacturing, Solar cells and modules manufacturing, UPS room without batteries (G-2) - entirely new hazard categories in 2026, reflecting modern building-services/medical/electronics occupancies not contemplated by the 2016 list

Automobiles and other motor vehicles powered by lithium/lithium-ion batteries manufacturing, Battery room with lithium-ion batteries, Diesel generator room, Hydrogenation rooms, Lithium ion battery manufacturing plants, LPG bullets, Oil fire boiler room/oil quenching tank, Oil transformer room, Paint booths, Paint/varnish storage, Server room, Tanker loading/unloading bay, Tunnel protection, UPS room with batteries (G-3) - a substantial new EV/lithium-ion-battery and data-centre-adjacent (server room) hazard category cluster with no 2016 counterpart at all
Outdoor oil transformer room (G-3 sub-category B) - not found in 2016
entries_present_in_2026_annex_b_but_not_.significance: The EV/lithium-ion battery and server-room additions in particular track directly with 2026's other new features noted elsewhere in this dataset (Group K Mixed Use, E-II Datacentre sub-occupancy) - 2026's Annex B was clearly revised specifically to catch up with building types (EV charging/parking, data centres) that were niche or nonexistent when NBC 2016 was drafted.
